question: A large monorepo team wants to organize .claude/rules/ into frontend/ and backend/ subdirectories for maintainability, for example .claude/rules/frontend/react.md and .claude/rules/backend/api.md. Will Claude Code still discover and load these rule files correctly?
options: A) Yes, because all .md files under .claude/rules/ are discovered recursively, so organizing them into subdirectories like frontend/ and backend/ does not prevent them from being found and evaluated.

B) No, because subdirectories under .claude/rules/ are reserved for skills and commands, so any .md files placed there are misinterpreted as skill or command artifacts and are simply skipped entirely.
C) No, because Claude Code only ever scans the top level of .claude/rules/ for .md files, so any rules placed in subdirectories such as frontend/ and backend/ are never discovered or loaded at all.

D) Only partially, because while the files are discovered, rules in subdirectories load unconditionally without respecting any paths frontmatter, so they are applied to all files, not just those matching the path constraints.
correct_answers: A) Yes, because all .md files under .claude/rules/ are discovered recursively, so organizing them into subdirectories like frontend/ and backend/ does not prevent them from being found and evaluated.
explanations: Correct. Claude Code recursively scans all .md files under .claude/rules/, so rules in subdirectories are discovered and loaded just like those in the top level. This allows teams to organize rules by subsystem without any loss of functionality.

Incorrect. Subdirectories under .claude/rules/ are not reserved for skills or commands; they are a supported way to organize rule files. Any .md files placed in them are properly recognized and processed as rules.

Incorrect. Claude Code performs recursive discovery of .md files under .claude/rules/, so rules in subdirectories like frontend/ and backend/ are still found and loaded. There is no limitation to the top-level directory.

Incorrect. The behavior of rule files (whether they are unconditional or path‑scoped) is determined entirely by the paths field in their frontmatter, not by their subdirectory location. Rules in subdirectories still respect any path constraints defined in their metadata.
